title: Tottenham 3–1 Coventry: first league win, decided after the equaliser
description: Maddison, Marmoush and Davies scored as Spurs finally won. Compare the goal timeline, possession, passing, shooting and defensive data, with clear limits on missing advanced metrics.

sections.heading: The result in one sentence
paragraphs: Tottenham beat Coventry 3–1 for their first league win of the season, restoring the lead nine minutes after the equaliser and only securing the two-goal margin in stoppage time.

sections.heading: Final result and timing
paragraphs: The match began at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on Monday 19 October 2026 at 20:00 BST, or 19:00 UTC; in Korea that was Tuesday 20 October at 04:00. Spurs led 1–0 at half-time and finished 3–1 ahead. This was a completed league match, not the still-published pre-match preview.

sections.heading: The four goals that shaped the result
paragraphs: James Maddison opened the scoring on 14 minutes. Jack Rudoni equalised on 49, before Omar Marmoush restored Tottenham's lead on 58. Ben Davies added the third at 90+6. The important distinction is timing: 3–1 was not the score for most of the contest, and the final margin should not hide Coventry's second-half equaliser.

sections.heading: More of the ball, but not a complete account of chance quality
paragraphs: Spurs had 65.4% possession to Coventry's 34.6%, with shots 16–12 and shots on target 5–1. They completed 499 of 559 passes; Coventry completed 222 of 287. Calculated completion rates are 89.27% and 77.35%. Those numbers support greater Tottenham ball circulation and more on-target output, but possession alone does not establish territorial dominance or prove which chances were best.

Coventry recorded 13 interceptions to Spurs' six, while fouls were 14 to 15. More interceptions can reflect defensive workload rather than a better overall defensive performance. The provider's successful-tackle ratios are 8/13 and 7/17; compare their stated denominator, not an assumed universal definition.

sections.heading: Scorers and goalkeeper context
paragraphs: Maddison, Marmoush and Davies supplied Tottenham's three goals; Rudoni scored Coventry's reply. The provider records no Tottenham save from one opposing shot on target, versus two Coventry saves from five. That produces 0% and 40% for this tiny sample, but it is not a fair goalkeeper-quality ranking without shot difficulty. No PSxG-based judgement is claimed.

sections.heading: What the preview question now tells us
paragraphs: The existing preview asked whether a Spurs side without a win in six league games could generate enough threat. Three goals and a first victory answer the outcome question positively. They do not, on their own, establish that a particular pressing or low-block tactic caused the result. Nor should an earlier uncalibrated baseline be rewritten as a successful calibrated forecast.

sections.heading: What changes after this win
paragraphs: The immediate change is the end of Tottenham's winless league start. The next test is whether this attacking output can be repeated rather than treating one result as proof that every problem has disappeared. The two-goal final margin and the period at 1–1 should both remain part of that assessment.

sections.heading: Data limits and sources
paragraphs: This report uses Premier League match 2645264, Tottenham's report and ESPN's recorded match statistics. xG, npxG, xA/xAG, PSxG, xT and PPDA were not present in the verified input used here, so none is fabricated. Derived percentages use observed counts and are rounded; differing provider definitions can produce different figures. The image's goals-by-half panel is explicitly not xG.
